newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-BOURSE SLOWS BUT INTEREST LINGERS.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-BOURSE SLOWS BUT INTEREST LINGERS.

text.p: The Tallinn stock exchange on
Friday saw moderate trade and dealers said share prices were
mostly holding recent gains on pent-up demand.
The Talse index rose 0.71 percent to 262.93 with 45.9
million kroons traded on the main list.
"Today's trade also released some of that pent-up demand of
recent weeks and encouraged spectulative interest," one dealer
said, noting it was still a relatively quiet market.
Tallinna Pank was most active on 11.9 million kroons to gain
1.15 kroons to close on 58.10 kroons.
"One big lot of 60,000 shares was moved in Tallinna Pank,
but it looked like a dealer filling a client's order and may
have been left over from Thursday," a dealer said.
Hansapank saw 11.8 million kroons change hands to move 1.35
kroons higher to close at 139.65 kroons.
Hoiupank saw 11.2 million kroons traded to slip to
136.06, 0.44 kroons lower compared to Thursday's close.
Both have been at the centre of merger speculation. Hansa
said it was seeking a partner to help it expand into Lithuania
while Hoiu said it would consider merging with any local bank.
"The talk of possible mergers is just an early start to the
expected merger process in Estonia," one trader said.
"The recent activity on the bourse has more to do with
having a market that suits speculators," another dealer said.
Trade on the free market was 5.9 million kroons on Friday
with Norma the most active at 4.95 million kroons,
adding 1.5 kroons to 71 kroons.
-- David Mardiste, Tallinn newsroom, +372 620 9202/1,
